hook.line: When someone does you a favour, "thanks" is good and praising the person is better. In Bogotá, telling someone their gesture was kind is how you show you noticed.

examples.en: How thoughtful of you. (to a friend)

examples.es: Fue muy amable de tu parte venir a verme.
examples.en: It was very kind of you to come and see me. (to a friend)
It was very generous of him to invite us.

examples.es: Es muy amable de su parte ayudarnos.
examples.en: It's very kind of you to help us. (formal)
That's very lovely of you. (to a friend)

rule:
English says "kind of you". Spanish says "kind of your part": the quality, then *de su parte* (for *usted*) or *de tu parte* (for *tú*).

*Muy amable de su parte.* To name the kind act, add an infinitive: *Fue muy amable de tu parte venir a verme.*

To praise someone not in the conversation, use *al* plus an infinitive: *Fue muy generoso al invitarnos*, "in inviting us".

Use *ser*, not *estar*: the kindness belongs to the act. Often *Muy amable* alone is enough.
smallPrint: Teachers call *al* plus an infinitive a temporal infinitive clause, "on doing".

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *de su parte* or *de tu parte* for someone you call *usted*, then type the whole sentence: That's very kind of you. *Muy amable ___.*
yourTurn.why: *Su parte* is the *usted* version of "of you".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: How thoughtful of you.
yourTurn.why: A *detalle* is a thoughtful touch, and *de tu parte* gives "of you".

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to a friend: It was very kind of you to come and see me.
yourTurn.answer: Fue muy amable de tu parte venir a verme.
yourTurn.why: The act comes last, as an infinitive: *venir a verme*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It was very generous of him to invite us.
yourTurn.why: For a third person, *al* plus an infinitive means "in inviting".

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal. *Fue muy amable de tu parte venir a verme.* Say, to someone you call *usted*: It was very kind of you to come and see me.
yourTurn.answer: Fue muy amable de su parte venir a verme.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: It was very kind of him to help me.
yourTurn.why: *Al* plus an infinitive; the *me* sticks to the end of *ayudar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish, to someone you call *usted*: How kind of you.
yourTurn.why: *Qué* plus the quality works like "how kind".

pitfalls.wrong: Eres muy amable de tu parte.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The phrase already says "of you", so no *eres* is needed.

pitfalls.wrong: Fue muy amable de ti venir a verme.
pitfalls.right: Fue muy amable de tu parte venir a verme.
pitfalls.why: Almost. English "of you" is *de tu parte* in Spanish, not *de ti*.

pitfalls.wrong: Estuvo muy amable de su parte.
pitfalls.right: Fue muy amable de su parte.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Praise for an act takes *ser* (*fue*), because the kindness belongs to the act, not to a passing mood.

personal: Remember something kind someone did for you recently. Thank them in one line, starting with *Fue muy amable de tu parte…* or *Muy amable de su parte*.
